summary.text: A 65-year-old woman presented in October 2021 with progressive upper abdominal pain, intermittent distension and weight loss of about 5-10 kg within a month. Examination showed slight upper abdominal tenderness. She was in good functional condition with ECOG 0, KPS 90 and NRS 0.

Gastroscopy showed an ulcerated infiltrative fundal lesion and biopsy showed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. CEA was 8.04 ng/mL with impaired liver tests. Staining was positive for CK7, negative for CK20 and HER2, Ki-67 about 80%, with MSS, low tumor mutational burden and PD-L1 CPS below 1; Claudin18.2 testing was not done. Diagnosis was stage IV gastric adenocarcinoma with multiple liver metastases.

First-line FOLFOX began in October 2021 and was stopped after three cycles because of CTCAE grade III gastrointestinal toxicity, bone marrow suppression and increasing tumor markers. After supportive care and MDT assessment, a long-term approach was advised and, given her lack of tolerance to 5-FU infusion, a personalized plan with oral fluoropyrimidine and PD-L1 blockade was chosen. In May 2022 maintenance weekly subcutaneous envafolimab 150 mg plus S-1 started and was well tolerated with only mild fatigue.

CT scans in June 2022, November 2022 and January 2023 showed multiple liver metastases. Sequential CT showed consistent shrinkage and long-term stabilization of the hepatic metastases with no new lesions throughout follow-up, and the abstract reports total regression of the primary gastric lesion. She kept ECOG 0 performance status and had 46 months of overall survival.

Discussion sentences (b00013-b00018) are interpretation and background; only index-patient statements (FOLFOX termination, absence of post-treatment biopsy and Claudin18.2 testing) were extracted.

Remission depth is a source conflict (complete remission and nonexistent disease vs near-complete radiologic remission with minimal residual abnormalities); both sides are review_only.
